title: What if the odd-news page had a play button? I'm letting an AI make one daily.
author: Alyosha2020
selftext:
An emu walks out of a zoo in Japan. People report an ostrich. You read the story, then try to stay loose longer than the actual bird.



That's the idea behind Oddday, a project I run: a daily odd-news page where you can get your hands on the story. An AI agent finds a real event, checks sources and builds a playful way to experience it. The format can be a game, a toy, a simulation or some strange interaction that fits the subject. Each day gets its own page on a tear-off calendar.



There are only two editions so far. The escaped emu became a chase with the real bird's roughly two hours as the target. Today's Fat Bear Week edition puts you under a waterfall catching salmon. A reported observation of a bear eating 40 salmon in one sitting supplies the target; the slower chomp as you get fatter is an invented game rule. The pages separate what actually happened from the silly part and link their sources.



For the AI-development side: the daily loop reads its previous notes, scouts stories, picks one, predicts how it will land, writes the interactive page, tests it and publishes. It also leaves a public diary of its choices, rejected ideas and mistakes. The brief allows different forms, so choosing what the reader should actually DO is part of its job too.



Today's diary admits that 'tap the fish' risks feeling like a hundred other games. That's the design question I'm interested in: can the interaction make a real story more memorable? It's early. The grades in the diary currently come from AI judges, not evidence that people enjoy it.



Readers can also send a weird story to the agent, get a note back on their ticket, and be credited if it becomes an edition. I like the possibility of tomorrow's page starting with something a reader noticed.



It's free to read and play: [https://oddday.alyobot.win/](https://oddday.alyobot.win/)

The editorial notebook: [https://oddday.alyobot.win/diary/](https://oddday.alyobot.win/diary/)



What kind of real-world story would you want to experience this way, and what would you let the reader do?
